extracted.intended_audience: authors, publishers, and literary community members interested in submitting books to or learning about the National Book Awards
extracted.subtask_description: Information and high-level criteria for books submitted to the National Book Awards, including which categories are honored, where to find eligibility and submission rules, the awards' mission, and medallion/image-rights provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award categories (scope of recognition)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Awards currently honor the best Fiction, Nonfiction, Poetry, Translated Literature, and Young People’s Literature, published each year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The National Book Awards recognize books published in the award year across these five categories. Historically other categories have existed, but current awards are limited to these. For category-specific eligibility rules and submission details, consult the Deadlines & Guidelines page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility and submissions (deadlines & guidelines)
rubrics_metrics.description: Deadlines & Guidelines: Eligibility, the submissions process, current prizes, guidelines, FAQ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This landing page references a separate Deadlines & Guidelines section that contains the concrete eligibility rules, submission procedures, and deadlines. Submitters must consult that section for itemized requirements (publisher eligibility, publication dates, formats accepted, entry procedures, fees, and timing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose / mission of the awards
rubrics_metrics.description: The National Book Awards were established in 1950 to celebrate the best writing in America. Since 1989, they have been overseen by the National Book Foundation, a nonprofit organization whose mission is to celebrate the best of American literature, to expand its audience, and to enhance the cultural value of great writing in America.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection is intended to honor outstanding American writing and expand readership and cultural recognition. This mission frames judging and outreach priorities; specific judging criteria are handled by the Foundation and its panels (details available on related pages).

rubrics_metrics.name: Medallions and digital image rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Seals and digital image rights are available for NBA Winner, Finalist, and Longlist titles. In addition to medallions for individual titles, we also offer medallions for 5 Under 35 honorees and Distinguished Contribution to American Letters medalists, which can be used for future or backlist titles, respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Winners, finalists, longlisted titles, 5 Under 35 honorees, and Distinguished Contribution medalists have access to official seals and digital assets for marketing. The page indicates availability and different usage (e.g., backlist use for Distinguished Contribution), but specific licensing terms and asset access instructions are on the medallions or guidelines pages.
